Types of chromosomes: autosomes, sex chromosomes and mtDNA

Source: R/gt_chromosome_types.R
gt_chromosome_types.Rd

The loci of a gen_tibble are on autosomes, on sex chromosomes (X and Y in XY systems, Z and W in ZW systems), on their pseudo-autosomal regions (PAR), or on the mitochondrial genome (MT, which can also be used for the genomes of other organelles, e.g. chloroplasts). gt_set_chromosome_types() declares the type of chromosomes that can not be recognised from their names (e.g. the numeric codes of PLINK), and the pseudo-autosomal regions of the X chromosome. gt_chromosome_types() lists the chromosomes with their type, and loci_chromosome_types() gives the type of each locus (e.g. to select the autosomal loci with select_loci_if()).

Usage

gt_set_chromosome_types(.x, types = NULL, chr_set = NULL, par = NULL)

gt_chromosome_types(.x)

loci_chromosome_types(.x, .col = "genotypes", ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_df'
loci_chromosome_types(.x, .col = "genotypes", ...)

# S3 method for class 'vctrs_bigSNP'
loci_chromosome_types(.x, .col = "genotypes", ...)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble (for loci_chromosome_types(), also its genotypes column).

types

a named character vector giving the type of chromosomes: its names are the chromosomes (as in loci_chromosomes(); for chromosomes stored as integer codes, their names, see gt_lookup_chromosomes()), and its values their types, one of "autosome", "X", "Y", "Z", "W", "PAR" and "MT". For example, c("23" = "X", "24" = "Y").

chr_set

the number of autosomes, as in PLINK's --chr-set, to declare the numeric codes of X, Y, XY and MT (see details), or "human". The types given in types take precedence.

par

the pseudo-autosomal regions of the X chromosome: either a build of the human genome ("b36", "b37", "b38", or their names "hg18", "hg19", "hg38"), whose boundaries apply to the chromosome of type "X", or a data frame with columns chromosome, start and end (positions, both included) giving the regions of each chromosome of type "X" that are pseudo-autosomal.

.col

the column to be used when a tibble (or grouped tibble is passed directly to the function). This defaults to "genotypes" and can only take that value. There is no need for the user to set it, but it is included to resolve certain tidyselect operations.

...

currently unused.

Value

gt_set_chromosome_types() returns the gen_tibble with the declared types; gt_chromosome_types() returns a tibble with columns chromosome, type and n_loci (the number of loci), with one row for each chromosome and type (an X chromosome with pseudo-autosomal regions has two rows); loci_chromosome_types() returns a factor with the type of each locus.

Details

Chromosomes are recognised from their names, regardless of case and of a prefix "chr", "chr_", "chromosome" or "chromosome_" (e.g. "X", "chrX" or "chromosome_x"): "X", "Y", "Z" and "W" are sex chromosomes; "XY", "PAR", "PAR1" and "PAR2" are pseudo-autosomal regions; and "MT", "M" and "0M" are the mitochondrial genome. All other chromosomes are autosomes. Numbers are never recognised, as their meaning depends on the species (PLINK codes the human X as 23, but chromosome 23 is an autosome in a dog): declare them with types or chr_set.

The types declared with gt_set_chromosome_types() are kept with the gen_tibble (they are saved by gt_save()); each call replaces the previous declaration, and a call without types, chr_set and par removes it. A declaration can also bring a recognised chromosome back among the autosomes (e.g. types = c(X = "autosome")).

Functions that pool loci and assume that they are on diploid autosomes only use the autosomal loci and the pseudo-autosomal regions, as PLINK does (e.g. for KING), and say how many loci they left out: the individual statistics indiv_het_obs(), indiv_inbreeding() and qc_report_indiv(); the pairwise statistics pairwise_king(), pairwise_ibs(), pairwise_dist(), pairwise_allele_sharing() and pairwise_grm(); gt_pca() (and the deprecated gt_pca_*SVD()) and gt_pcadapt(); gt_extract_f2(), gt_admixture() and gt_snmf(); windows_indiv_roh(); and the population statistics (pop_fst(), pop_fis(), pop_het_obs(), pop_het_exp(), pop_gene_div(), pop_global_stats(), pairwise_pop_fst(), nwise_pop_pbs(), pop_tajimas_d(), the site frequency spectra pop_sfs(), pairwise_pop_sfs(), nwise_pop_sfs(), bootstrap_pop_sfs(), and their windows_*() and jackknife_*() versions), whose results by locus or by window then cover the autosomal loci only. gt_pseudohaploid() also tests autosomal loci. The functions that return one value per locus (loci_*(), qc_report_loci()), LD clumping and pruning, and imputation use all loci, without treating the sex chromosomes of males as haploid. To include a sex chromosome or the mitochondrial genome in the analyses that use autosomes only, declare it as an autosome.

PLINK codes chromosomes with numbers: with n autosomes, X is n+1, Y is n+2, the pseudo-autosomal region of X ("XY") is n+3, and MT is n+4 (23 to 26 in humans, as set by --chr-set n). chr_set = n declares those codes; chr_set = "human" is chr_set = 22, plus the codes of EIGENSOFT for the mitochondrial genome (90) and XY (91).

PLINK's --split-x moves the loci of the pseudo-autosomal regions of the human X chromosome to the chromosome "XY", using the boundaries of a build of the human genome: a locus on X is in a pseudo-autosomal region if its position is at most the last position of PAR1, or at least the first position of PAR2. par gives the type "PAR" to those loci without changing their chromosome: "b36" (or "hg18") uses 2709521 and 154584237, "b37" (or "hg19") 2699520 and 154931044, and "b38" (or "hg38") 2781479 and 155701383, as PLINK.

References

Purcell S, Neale B, Todd-Brown K, Thomas L, Ferreira MAR, Bender D, Maller J, Sklar P, de Bakker PIW, Daly MJ, Sham PC (2007) PLINK: a tool set for whole-genome association and population-based linkage analyses. American Journal of Human Genetics, 81(3), 559-575. doi:10.1086/519795

Examples

bed_file <- system.file("extdata", "pop_a.bed", package = "tidypopgen")
example_gt <- gen_tibble(bed_file,
  backingfile = tempfile("pop_a_"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

# chromosome 23 is taken as an autosome
gt_chromosome_types(example_gt)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   chromosome type     n_loci
#>   <chr>      <fct>     <int>
#> 1 1          autosome     11
#> 2 2          autosome      3
#> 3 3          autosome      1
#> 4 23         autosome      1

# declare the human codes of PLINK: 23 is the X chromosome
example_gt <- gt_set_chromosome_types(example_gt, chr_set = "human")
gt_chromosome_types(example_gt)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   chromosome type     n_loci
#>   <chr>      <fct>     <int>
#> 1 1          autosome     11
#> 2 2          autosome      3
#> 3 3          autosome      1
#> 4 23         X             1
loci_chromosome_types(example_gt)
#>  [1] autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome
#>  [9] autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome autosome X       
#> Levels: autosome X Y Z W PAR MT

# keep the autosomal loci only
example_gt %>%
  select_loci_if(loci_chromosome_types(genotypes) == "autosome") %>%
  count_loci()
#> [1] 15
